newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up slightly, gains more on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up slightly, gains more on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended with modest gains Wednesday in a lackluster session, then moved higher on ACCESS after a slightly bullish weekly AGA stock report, industry sources said.
December eased 0.1 cent to close at $2.645 per million British thermal units. January settled 0.7 cent higher at $2.65. Most other deferreds ended up by about one-half cent.

"We've been languishing in this area for a while. If the AGA number is real, it was more constructive than I expected, which probably means we're more likely to test the higher end of the range," said one East Coast trader.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas inventories fell last week by 22 bcf, well-below an earlier Reuter poll showing most expected flat to slightly higher stocks for the week.
On ACCESS, December climbed 3.5 cents to $2.68 shortly after the report.
But despite the cold this week that roused the bulls, traders said forecasts for more seasonal weather next week tempered any upside enthusiasm.

Technical traders agreed the market was range bound, with trendline support in December at $2.59-2.60 and better buying likely at $2.53. Resistance remained at $2.75 and then at the $2.88 contract high.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices were down slightly Wednesday to about the $2.70 area. Midwest prices slipped more than a nickel to about $2.60. Cold weather firmed New York city gate swing gas by about 10 cents to the $3.50-60 area. December gas in New York was still quoted at about $1.25 over the screen, or in the low-$3.90s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip edged up one-half cent to $2.182. NYMEX said 26,955 Hub contracts traded, down from Tuesday's revised tally of 39,999.

NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed 18 cents higher at $1.51 after setting a new contract high of $1.55. Deferred contracts were untraded. NYMEX said 16 Alberta contracts traded versus 10 lots on Monday.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded for the fifth consecutive day. December ended unchanged at $2.45.
On the KCBT, December finished one-half cent higher at $2.47, while deferreds settled down by about one cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.6 cent to 17.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
